findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry datetime keys
findings.body: This endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the value of that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a `datetime`, not a numeric value, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` will raise a TypeError while constructing cursors and return a 500. The optimized paginator needs datetime key conversion equivalent to `DateTimePaginator`, or this endpoint must continue to use a datetime-aware paginator.

findings.title: Deploying this script against existing set-backed buffers causes Redis WRONGTYPE failures
findings.body: Existing buffered segment keys were created as Redis SETs by the previous version. This script now executes `ZCARD` and `ZUNIONSTORE` on those same keys. Redis does not permit ZSET commands on SET values, so any trace with an in-flight pre-deployment buffer will make the script fail with WRONGTYPE, failing span processing until the old key expires (up to `redis_ttl`, normally an hour). A rollout-compatible migration/fallback or a versioned key namespace is required.

findings.title: max_segment_spans configuration is no longer honored
findings.body: `max_segment_spans` remains a constructor parameter and instance attribute, but the only enforcement was removed from `_load_segment_data`; the Lua script instead always retains 1000 members. Deployments that configure a different limit now silently get a hard-coded retention policy, and segments over the configured limit are emitted rather than skipped as before. Either pass the configured limit to Lua and enforce it there, or remove/change the public configuration deliberately.

findings.title: Reducing redirect traversal depth can split deep traces into separate segments
findings.body: The redirect-chain traversal limit was reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose parent/child buffers form a chain deeper than 1,000, resolution stops before reaching the actual segment root; subsequent spans are merged into an intermediate buffer and flushed as a separate segment. This changes the prior supported depth and produces incorrect segment assignments for deep traces.
